items.root_cause: The c744ba pending-pair hold is judged afresh each day from that day's sanity flags, and its wow half ('unexplained: a NEW price at the cheapest store') compares against the previous COMPARISON file, not against what was published. So a wrong crown the pair names on day 1 becomes the baseline that explains itself on day 2, the pair decays to a single outlier flag, and the cell publishes while its ledger entry is still pending. Reachability underneath it: a Family Fare Weekly Ad line can name a household product without its class noun, and every defence on the road (the commodity exclude, audit-household-in-food's $HOUSEHOLD_SIGNAL) is a noun or brand vocabulary; the store's own department, which the flyer-link lane records, is read by nothing that gates the board.

root_fix.what: A pending pair PERSISTS for its exact claim until the ledger closes it or the claim leaves the board, instead of being re-derived from one day's flags.
root_fix.exact_change: In Get-TcPendingPairCells (flag-verify-lib.ps1) accept the flags of EVERY guards-<date>.json on or before the board date and no older than the claim's own ad_from (or, for an everyday claim with no ad_from, the ledger entry's first-seen day, capped at 7 days back), not only the newest. A crown is named when, on ANY of those days, the same claim key (id|store|item|per_unit, the key the function already matches on) carried both an unverified 'outlier' and a 'wow' reading 'unexplained: a NEW price at the cheapest store', AND its ledger entry is still pending today. A closed 'match' still releases it; a changed claim (different item or per_unit) is a new claim and starts over. audit-flag-verification.ps1 lines 90-94 today pick ONE file ('Sort-Object Name -Descending | Select-Object -First 1'); pass the list instead, print how many files and which days it read, and say BLIND when none. The guards files are 8 in the 14 days to 09-28, so the read stays cheap.

items.subject: triage residual: a name that cannot state its form is routed by name alone (d493dd)
evidence: out/coverage-gaps.json (generated 2026-09-28 08:24, classified_against candidates-2026-09-28.json): 316 gaps, 18 BASIS-NULL. By reading all 18: 16 sit on the right commodity with a size the engine cannot express ('' from a size range such as 'Dawn dishwashing liquid, 38 to 67 fl. oz.', 'lb' on each-sold kale and pie pumpkin, '$0.56/oz', 'Fresh Meat Counter', '12 ct' on string-cheese, '2 ea' phyllo); 2 are wrong products whose names DO state their form (Aldi 'Bremer Angus Cheeseburger Pita Melt 13.5 OZ' on pita-bread; Hy-Vee 'apple juice, 12 fl. oz. concentrate' on apple-juice). 0 are the d493dd class (a name that cannot state its form, claimed first by a commodity that cannot price it while another would).

candidates-2026-09-28.json holds priced rows only (unit_price, basis): 0 BASIS-NULL and 0 null per_unit records, so the row-level count the residual asks for cannot be read from any artifact; coverage-gaps re-derives BASIS-NULL only for store cells that are empty.
items.root_cause: The engine routes first-match-wins by name and prices only afterwards, so a row whose size kind fits a later commodity is unpriced on its first match and never offered to the later one. Unpriced rows are recorded only where they leave a store cell empty (coverage-gaps BASIS-NULL), so a shadowed occurrence is invisible.
items.root_fix_none_because: One occurrence ever (Hy-Vee Dole Mandarin Oranges on fruit-cups, board 09-23), closed by d493dd's fruit-cups narrowing, and 0 of 18 BASIS-NULL gaps on today's board are the class. Measuring shadowed rows needs a new per-row emit from compare-deals (a lifted, not-standalone engine, gr-04), which costs more than one occurrence in five boards justifies.
items.leaves_open: Shadowed occurrences (a row unpriced on its first match while another row fills that store cell) cannot be counted from any artifact. Also found, outside this class: the Aldi 'Bremer ... Pita Melt' rows are wrong products on pita-bread, currently harmless because they are unpriced.
items.leaves_open_occurrences: 1 gap-level occurrence over 2026-09-23..2026-09-28 (the mandarin jar, fixed); 0 today. Owned by watch:grocery/audit-coverage-gaps.ps1, whose BASIS-NULL listing is how d493dd found the first one.
items.resolution_note: No code change. Re-measured on today's coverage-gaps: 18 BASIS-NULL gaps, 16 are right-commodity sizes the engine cannot express, 2 are wrong products that name their own form (Aldi Pita Melt, Hy-Vee juice concentrate), and 0 are the name-cannot-state-its-form class. Rows hidden behind a priced row cannot be counted without a new engine emit, and one occurrence in five boards does not pay for one. Reopen if a second BASIS-NULL of this shape appears in coverage-gaps.
